questions.question: `SELECT * FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)` returns no rows, even though some customers have never ordered. What is the most likely cause?
options: NOT IN cannot be used with subqueries in MySQL
The subquery returns at least one NULL customer_id, making every NOT IN comparison UNKNOWN
The orders table has no index on customer_id
NOT IN only works with literal lists
questions.explanation: x NOT IN (..., NULL) expands to a chain of <> comparisons ending in x <> NULL, which is UNKNOWN, so no row qualifies. NOT EXISTS is NULL-safe.

questions.question: How do you get FULL OUTER JOIN semantics in MySQL exactly, without collapsing genuinely duplicate rows?
options: Use the FULL OUTER JOIN keyword, supported since MySQL 8.0
Use a CROSS JOIN with a WHERE clause
LEFT JOIN UNION ALL the RIGHT JOIN rows where the left key IS NULL
Use two INNER JOINs combined with INTERSECT
questions.explanation: MySQL has no FULL OUTER JOIN. A LEFT JOIN plus only the unmatched rows from a RIGHT JOIN, combined with UNION ALL, is exact and avoids UNION's deduplication.

questions.question: A query does `customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.total > 1000`. What happens to customers with no orders?
options: They are dropped, because o.total is NULL for them and the WHERE condition is not true
They appear with NULL order columns
They appear once per order in the table
questions.explanation: WHERE filters after the join; a null-rejecting condition on the right table effectively turns the LEFT JOIN into an inner join. Move the filter into ON to keep them.

questions.question: Which statement about joins in MySQL is correct?
options: A self join requires a separate copy of the table
CROSS JOIN cannot take an ON clause
JOIN, INNER JOIN and CROSS JOIN are syntactic equivalents in MySQL
questions.explanation: In MySQL these three keywords are interchangeable; the presence of a join condition determines whether you get a filtered join or a Cartesian product.
